classification.difficultyReason: Infer the square box dimensions from the cylinder diameter and subtract the cylinder volume from the box volume.

content.prompt: A cylindrical vase of radius $5\text{ cm}$ and height $14\text{ cm}$ just fits into a box. Find:

spec.description: An upright cylinder fits snugly inside a square-based box, sharing its height. The projected circular ends touch the four sides of the horizontal square faces. The top centre is marked and the hidden rear bottom semicircle is dashed. Ordinary source blue and red marks are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The box has square base side equal to the cylinder diameter and height equal to the cylinder height. No numerical measurements are printed in the diagram.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and geometric relationships are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the volume of the cylinder, correct to two decimal places

answer.worked:
The box has a square base of side $2\times5=10\text{ cm}$ and height $14\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{box}}&=Ah\\V_{\text{box}}&=(10\times10)\times14\\V_{\text{box}}&=1400\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the volume of unused space inside the box, correct to two decimal places

answer.short:
$300.44\text{ cm}^3$

Subtract the cylinder volume from the box volume.
